decision_provenance.label: initial-question
visible_user_messages:
you'll see some notes computer player (AI) tuning in the civ6-gameplay skill and romanholiday's ai mod. I want for us to add some guidance for the AI on how to play well with CSC. the main things I've been thinking of are:

- guiding good placement of quarters, ie adjacent to both base and specialty materials, as well as a sales district if possible
- later placing sales districts adjacent to quarters
- improving materials resources adjacent to quarters
- if possible, understanding the benefits of services and which quarters to prioritise in order to pursue certain benefits, etc.

in my mind, the adjacency bonuses given during district placement should already encourage good placement, but not sure the AI will know how to read our custom adjacency system, unless it just evaluates the total adjacency output, regardless of the method of granting it?

what is feasible?
final_answer_excerpts:
**We can give the AI useful CSC guidance. District-to-district placement and broad Quarter priorities look quite feasible; exact base/specialty material placement is the main technical uncertainty.**

Your adjacency intuition is sound **if the bonus reaches the engine’s placement evaluator**. CSC’s human placement preview does not establish that it does.

In the current implementation, [the UI adds CSC’s calculated preview](<C:/Users/Shadow/Documents/Firaxis ModBuddy/Civilization VI/Henno Mods/Civ Supply Chains/Lua_UI/Adjacencies/AdjacencyBonusSupport.lua>), while gameplay applies bonuses through properties on existing, completed districts. There is no visible connection passing that preview calculation into the native AI’s evaluation of an empty tile. **My working assumption is that the AI cannot anticipate these custom bonuses reliably**, though a controlled test is needed to confirm it.

| Your objective | Feasibility |
|---|---|
| Place Quarters beside sales districts | Strong candidate using native placement signals |
| Later place sales districts beside Quarters | Strong candidate using the same technique in reverse |
| Place Quarters beside the correct base **and** specialty materials | Harder; exact matching needs an experimental bridge |
| Improve adjacent material resources | Ordinary improvement incentives can help; valuing the extra benefits to the Quarter needs testing |
| Prioritise Quarters for particular Services or strategies | Feasible as weighted preferences; full supply-chain planning is much harder |

**The most useful RomanHoliday technique is a custom scoring yield.** Its public source adds native adjacency rules producing `YIELD_RH_PLACEMENT`, then gives that yield an AI valuation. Examples encourage Industrial Zones beside Aqueducts and Aqueducts beside Industrial Zones. This provides a precedent for teaching both build orders without adding real Production, Food or Gold. The public repository is marked as an older version, so this is evidence of the technique rather than verification of current RHAI compatibility. [Placement rules](https://github.com/Roman-Holiday/RHAI/blob/main/core/Strategies/Internal_Strat2.sql), [yield registration and weighting](https://github.com/Roman-Holiday/RHAI/blob/main/core/Strategies/Relic_Strat.sql).

For CSC, we could author our own equivalent:

- Bakers’ Quarter values adjacency to its sales districts.
- Commercial Hubs and Entertainment Complexes value adjacency to Bakers’ Quarters.
- Tailors’ Quarters and their Harbor, Holy Site, Commercial Hub and Theater Square customers receive corresponding signals.

We can generate those relationships from CSC’s existing tags, including unique replacements. These would still be preferences: a Harbor should retain its other placement considerations, for example. CSC would not need RomanHoliday installed.

**Materials are the difficult part because native adjacency rules cannot express CSC’s exact resource groups.** The installed schema supports particular districts, improvements, terrain and features, but resource matching is limited to generic resources and resource classes. It has no selector for “Bakers’ base materials” or a specific resource type.

We could approximate this with farms, plantations and pastures, but that would miss unimproved resources and sometimes favour the wrong resources. It also misses an important distinction you raised: **three base materials are not necessarily better than one base plus one specialty material**, even when their immediate adjacency yield is higher. The second arrangement can enable later Services.

Our Lua can readily calculate that richer score. The unresolved question is how to make the native AI consume it *before placement*. Simply writing another plot property does not establish that connection. A property-gated custom yield is worth testing, but I would treat it as an experiment rather than promise it works.

**Builders have a similar distinction between direct and indirect benefits.** Improving a resource already has ordinary incentives, and CSC’s additional yields on the improved tile may strengthen them. However, the improvement can also increase yields elsewhere or complete a Service’s requirements. We have not established that the builder evaluator anticipates those consequences.

Increasing builder production alone would therefore be incomplete guidance. The useful test is whether an AI builder chooses a material resource beside a Quarter over an otherwise comparable resource elsewhere.

**For Services, we can encode their value without expecting the AI to discover every dependency.** Services are granted automatically, so the guidance should target the enabling Quarter, buildings, improvements and customer placement.

For example:

- Growth-oriented play can give greater weight to Bakers’ and its Storekeeper chain.
- Naval play can favour Tailors’ and the Textile Workshop–Lighthouse relationship.
- Culture-oriented play can favour supplied Fashion House

decision_provenance.label: map-variation
visible_user_messages: okay, so this modding topic is new to me, so explain a bit more (and research where you have to). what is the overall flow for map generation? which intervention points exist, and how do they interact? what does TAR do, as it says on its workshop page that it's compatible with a number of other map script mods. and then what does Suk's Oceans do?
final_answer_excerpts:
**Civ VI’s map generation is a sequence of cooperating scripts.** A map mod can control the shape of the world while another mod handles resources, provided they agree on how those pieces connect.

TAR and Sukritact’s Oceans demonstrate two different intervention points: **TAR changes resource placement during generation; Oceans revises parts of the completed world during game initialization.** I checked their installed code as well as their Workshop descriptions.

**The normal generation flow**

Using Gathering Storm’s Continents script as a concrete example, the sequence is:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["Load settings and modded database rules"] --> B["Generate land, water, terrain, hills and mountains"]
    B --> C["Add rivers, lakes, features, natural wonders and coastal lowlands"]
    C --> D["Place resources"]
    D --> E["Choose starting locations and adjust their surroundings"]
    E --> F["Place tribal villages"]
    F --> G["Run gameplay initialization scripts"]
    G --> H["Normal play begins"]
```

A few details matter here:

- **The database supplies the rules.** It defines which resources exist, their placement frequencies, and which terrains and features can support them. Resource mods can change these rules before placement begins.
- **The selected map script coordinates the work.** For example, `Continents.lua` calls shared helpers such as `ResourceGenerator` and `AssignStartingPlots`. A custom map script can reuse those helpers, replace some, or implement its own.
- **Resource placement precedes start selection.** This lets the starting-position system consider the resources already present.
- **Starting-position code can change resources again.** It can remove resources from a starting tile or add resources around starts, including adjustments for Balanced and Legendary starts. The first resource-placement pass therefore isn’t necessarily the final distribution.
- Strategic resources are already placed at this point; research later reveals them.

That sequence comes directly from the installed [Continents script](<C:/Program Files (x86)/Steam/steamapps/common/Sid Meier's Civilization VI/DLC/Expansion2/Maps/Continents.lua:31>) and its starting-position helper. Other map scripts can change the sequence.

Also, the game’s **named continents and connected landmasses are different things**. One connected landmass can contain several named continents. “Four luxuries per continent” refers to those continent regions.

**Where mods can intervene**

| Intervention | What it controls | How it interacts with other mods |
|---|---|---|
| Database changes | Eligible terrain/features, frequencies, available resource types | Several mods can contribute rules, although conflicting edits still need resolving. |
| A custom map script | The generation sequence and potentially every stage | Chooses which shared generators to use. Only one selected map script coordinates that map. |
| A shared-generator replacement | One stage, such as resource placement | Works with scripts that call that generator; competes with other replacements of the same file. |
| Starting-position changes | Start selection and nearby balancing | Can revise resources placed earlier; custom start systems may bypass the standard one. |
| A gameplay initialization pass | The already generated world | Avoids replacing map scripts, but its edits happen after start selection and can interact with other initialization passes. |

An important distinction is that **adding a Lua file doesn’t automatically insert it between two generation stages**. Something must execute it: the map script, a shared generator, or the gameplay-script loading system.

Likewise, load order can determine which replacement takes effect, but it doesn’t automatically merge two different resource generators.

**What TAR actually does**

TAR has three components:

1. It adds the **Plentiful** and **Truly Abundant** setup options.
2. It changes database rules: broader terrain/feature eligibility, changes to sea-resource variety and frequency, and harvesting rules.
3. It supplies a replacement **`ResourceGenerator.lua`**, retaining the standard `ResourceGenerator.Create(...)` interface.

Its Workshop page describes additional sea-resource distribution changes and lists PerfectWorld6, YnAMP, Detailed Worlds, Got Lakes and Fantastical among compatible map mods. Those improvements also apply when using ordinary resource settings. [TAR Workshop description](https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=901009089)

**That compatibility list makes sense because a custom map script needn’t replace resource placement.** It can generate an unusual landscape, then call the shared resource generator. In that arrangement, TAR supplies the resource-placement step.

So my earlier warning needs that qualification: **replacing the resource generator does not inherently conflict with custom map scripts. The direct conflict is with another mod trying to supply that same generator.*

decision_provenance.label: durable-objective
visible_user_messages:
okay nice, so we have some more visibility now and hopefully we can turn the Civ VI into less of a black box. but let's just take time to pin (pls write this down as a durable objective) what we want to achieve with the Civ AI:



the main objective is to make the AI competent at using CSC's supply chain mechanics to extract increased total benefit to their empire, and ideally to use the supply chains to extract value from their lands and empire toward their overall victory progress and priorities.



practically speaking, I think this objective implies a few things, most related to the spatial planning puzzle of CSC's supply chains:



- favorable placement of quarters adjacent to materials mapped to their supply chain. at the very least Base materials, but sites with both Base and Specialty materials adjacent are of particular interest.
- sites adjacent to rivers are also of interest due to the production adjacency bonus that brings
- sites adjacent to customer districts (or given that quarters unlock earlier than many customer districts, sites that leave space for / allow for the development of customer districts)
- the above three sources of adjacency bonuses for quarters should probably be combined together and measured against a threshold where we give different priority / weight to sites with combined +3, +4, +5, etc. potential. this is where buying tiles to secure these sites could be worth it.
- placement of customer districts adjacent to quarters, but in a way that is balanced with other good placement options for those districts. a +4 Campus adjacent to a mountain clump should probably not be placed adjacent to an ApothecariesQ instead where it only earns +1. if it can be both, then that's of course great.
- improvement, retention and repair of materials adjacent to quarters
- construction of producer and customer buildings in quarters and customer districts
- matching of service effects with AI player priorities and needs
- repair of pillaged quarters, customer districts and materials improvements



possibly other things I'm forgetting. do you agree? anything I'm missing?
final_answer_excerpts:
Yes—I agree. **The goal is worthwhile, functioning supply chains that strengthen the empire**, with adjacency and Quarter counts serving as intermediate measures.

Saved as the [durable CSC AI objective](</C:/Users/Shadow/Documents/Firaxis ModBuddy/Civilization VI/Henno Mods/project/docs/integrations/csc-ai-objectives.md>), linked from the project index, tuning documentation and memory.

Your list covers the core capabilities. I’d add four considerations:

- **Whole-chain opportunity cost:** tile Gold, production, Builder charges, district capacity and competing investments. A +5 site may be worse than a +3 site that becomes productive much sooner.
- **Capacity and sequencing:** recognise when finishing buildings or repairing an existing chain is more valuable than placing another Quarter.
- **Coordination:** avoid reserving the same future space for incompatible districts; exploit shared customers where useful without double-counting benefits.
- **Replanning and resilience:** respond to capture, material loss and changing priorities. Preserving supplies should be a strong preference, while still allowing genuinely better redevelopment.

For the combined adjacency score, I’d retain two separate assessments: **benefit available now** and **credible future potential**. Then account for the time and investment needed to realise the latter. Both sites deserve particular attention, but their Specialty potential should not outweigh an otherwise weak development plan automatically.

I recorded these additions as proposals, distinct from your confirmed objectives. The +3/+4/+5 bands remain candidates to investigate rather than fixed rules.

decision_provenance.label: offline-first
visible_user_messages: okay, so how do we now best proceed here? what's next on the roadmap and what does Astra think of using REA? do we need to keep testing against live games or can we use REA to work offline against gamecore more?
final_answer_excerpts:
**We should do more mechanism discovery offline now, followed by fewer, more decisive live tests. Astra agrees.**

Astra considers REA useful for following values and arguments across functions and retaining the supporting evidence. It helps explain GameCore’s logic, but **it doesn’t execute a saved world or establish how the AI behaves under actual conditions**.

The next steps are:

1. **Finish a bounded offline investigation.** Check the repaired site reader’s UI bindings, then determine whether one planner-selected material improvement can reach a native economic job—with the correct AI, target, available Builder and cleanup. Use REA for missing links; reuse what we already know. Establish actual Builder support before exploring an entire military-operation system.

2. **Complete the zero-turn site capture.** Once its bindings pass preflight, collect the candidate sites and adjacency information from the existing save. This can proceed independently of the native-job investigation.

3. **Prove one useful action.** If the interface looks viable, test one existing Builder improving one mapped material. Require correct ownership, physical completion and release of reservations. If the route remains unsupported, continue through our working guidance and guarded assistance.

The division is:

| Offline analysis can establish | Live games must establish |
|---|---|
| Consumers, calculations, argument flow and code-level conditions | Actual activation, state and effective values |
| Potential side effects and cancellation paths | Assignment, pathfinding, completion and cleanup |
| Which controls deserve testing | Whether they improve functioning supply chains enough to justify their costs |

**We don’t need another long campaign yet.** The immediate work is offline, then a small validation session. Longer matched Basic/RH games come after we have a useful mechanism to evaluate.

I’ve saved Astra’s advice and clarified that sequence in the [roadmap](</C:/Users/Shadow/Documents/Firaxis ModBuddy/Civilization VI/Henno Mods/project/docs/integrations/csc-ai-roadmap.md>).

decision_provenance.label: latest-closure
visible_user_messages: give me an overview of the night's progress
final_answer_excerpts:
We made progress in **placement, diagnosis and engine visibility**, but the latest tuning **hasn’t improved the overall supply-chain result yet**.

The customer-aware RH test finished turn 150. Compared with the previous selective RH run:

| At turn 150 | Previous | New |
|---|---:|---:|
| Quarters | 53 | 56 |
| With working Base materials | 19 | 15 |
| With working Both materials | 4 | 2 |
| Functioning upstream producers | 38 | 39 |
| Functioning supply chains | 3 | 2 |
| Functioning assisted chains | 0 | 1 |
| Tile-acquisition cost | 195 Gold | 200 Gold |

These are observed operating structures, not measured Service payments. Also, **85 Gold of the new spending occurred at turn 149**, leaving that investment unfinished at the endpoint. [Detailed results](C:/Users/Shadow/.codex/visualizations/2026/10/11/01a12a24-6714-7540-8d23-154b092106fe/customer-aware-planner-v2-20261101/outcomes-final150.json).

We confirmed several useful things:

- **The Base-only “+4 or better” placement route works.** It can secure a legal site with a specific customer path.
- **One assisted chain became operational at 119** and remained working at every subsequent checkpoint through 150. It developed a different valid Mill from the planned one.
- **Good customer geometry doesn’t ensure construction.** Another completed Quarter acquired its Wind Mill but still lacked the adjacent Granary at 150.
- **Future customer reservations are only promises.** The AI put a Theater Square on one reserved Holy Site plot.
- **Material loss is now directly attributable in one case:** a Builder harvested the selected, unimproved Cattle for a Farm job. This was confirmed from coordinates, operation logs and resource disappearance—not inferred from a missing resource.

Astra recommends focusing next on **native Quarter placement scoring**. Most Quarters still come from the AI itself; only 10 of the 50 clearly native sites had working Base supply at the endpoint. That includes both placement and later maintenance failures.

The ensuing Ghidra trace found a promising concrete route: **native district adjacencies enter pre-placement scoring, and that scoring path includes custom yields with configurable, nonzero weights**. This could support Quarter-specific mapped-resource guidance instead of generic bonus-resource encouragement. Actual candidate-score and placement responses remain untested.

We also identified the UI helper startup fault and applied the reviewed source repair plus clearer prerequisite diagnostics. The staged versions passed 47 focused Lua checks; **post-promotion canonical tests and fresh cold-start validation remain pending**.

The game closed normally, the original installation and settings were restored, and over **96 GiB** of abandoned Ghidra copies were cleared with automatic cleanup added.

**The goal is paused.** No further game or investigation is running.
